key_insight: Hybrid quantum-classical query algorithms lose the full quantum speedup when quantum subroutines are capped at q queries, yielding tight scaling laws that interpolate between classical and quantum limits.
engineering_relevance: These bounds tell system designers how much query savings remain available in practical hybrid workflows where intermediate measurements and resets are unavoidable.
method: Derive matching upper and lower bounds in the query model for phase estimation, amplitude estimation, search, and AND-OR trees.
Analyze measurement transcripts with a progress measure to quantify how distinguishable the algorithm’s outcomes become over time.
For AND-OR trees, combine separate classical-information and quantum-information progress measures to handle mixed computation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tight Θ-bounds for four benchmark problems and notes the lower bounds are optimal up to constant factors across the full range from q=1 to the unrestricted quantum limit.
watch_item: The guarantees are model-specific and rely on query complexity assumptions, so real hardware effects or non-query costs may change practical performance.
paper_title: Tight bounds for hybrid quantum-classical query algorithms
